+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats — cycle-129 D-4.5 (AC-2.5)
+#
+# The five C-TEAM rows left constraints.json; generate-constraints.sh omits the
+# "## Agent Teams" table when the class is empty and renders it when rows
+# exist; lint-invariants.sh fails when the kernel and the registry disagree.
+# The generator runs against a fixture tree (it resolves its inputs relative
+# to the working directory), never against the live kernel.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    GEN="$R/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh"
+    LINT="$R/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh"
+    F="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/tree"
+    mkdir -p "$F/.claude/loa" "$F/.claude/data" "$F/.claude/templates"
+    cp -R "$R/.claude/templates/constraints" "$F/.claude/templates/constraints"
+    cp "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+    cp "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+# A kernel that still carries the pre-cycle-129 Agent Teams block, placed
+# between the merge constraints and the Agent-Network section as it was.
+add_team_block() {
+    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
+import sys
+p = sys.argv[1]
+s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
+anchor = "## Agent-Network Primitives"
+block = ("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |\n|------|-----|\n"
+         "<!-- @constraint-generated: start agent_teams_constraints | hash:0000000000000000 -->\n"
+         "<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->\n"
+         "| MUST stale row | stale |\n"
+         "<!-- @constraint-generated: end agent_teams_constraints -->\n\n")
+assert s.count(anchor) == 1
+open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(anchor, block + anchor))
+PY
+}
+
+add_team_row() {
+    jq '.constraints += [{"id":"C-TEAM-901","name":"fixture_row","category":"agent_teams","rule_type":"MUST",
+        "text":"fixture rule","text_variants":{"claude-loa-md":"MUST fixture rule"},"why":"fixture why","order":0,
+        "layers":[{"target":"claude-loa-md","section":"agent_teams_constraints","render_as":"table_row"}],
+        "severity":"low","source_incident":"#0"}]' "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json" > "$F/c.json"
+    mv "$F/c.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+}
+
+gen() { (cd "$F" && bash "$GEN" --section "${1:-agent_teams_constraints}"); }
+
+@test "LI-1 constraints.json carries no C-TEAM rows and no agent_teams_constraints layer" {
+    run jq '[.constraints[] | select((.id | startswith("C-TEAM")) or any(.layers[]?; .section == "agent_teams_constraints"))] | length' \
+        "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$output" = "0" ]
+}
+
+@test "LI-2 the live kernel carries neither the Agent Teams heading nor its marker" {
+    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-3 the generator removes a leftover Agent Teams block when the class is empty" {
+    add_team_block
+    grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    run gen
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    # The neighbouring sections survive with one blank line between them.
+    grep -qF '<!-- @constraint-generated: end merge_constraints -->' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    run grep -c '^## Agent-Network Primitives$' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    [ "$output" = "1" ]
+    run diff <(sed -n '/end merge_constraints/,/^## Agent-Network/p' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md") \
+             <(printf '%s\n' '<!-- @constraint-generated: end merge_constraints -->' '' '## Agent-Network Primitives')
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "LI-4 pruning is idempotent: a second run leaves the kernel byte-identical" {
+    add_team_block
+    gen
+    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/first.md"
+    run gen
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    cmp "$F/first.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-5 the generator renders the table when the class has rows" {
+    add_team_block
+    add_team_row
+    run gen
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    grep -qxF '| MUST fixture rule | fixture why |' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    ! grep -qF 'MUST stale row' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-6 rows without the heading block fail loudly and leave the kernel untouched" {
+    add_team_row
+    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"
+    run gen
+    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Missing markers"*"agent_teams_constraints"* ]]
+    cmp "$F/before.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-7 a marker block with foreign text above it is an error, not a silent deletion" {
+    add_team_block
+    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
+import sys
+p = sys.argv[1]
+s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
+s = s.replace("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |", "## Agent Teams\n\nOperator prose that is not a table.\n\n| Rule | Why |")
+open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
+PY
+    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"
+    run gen
+    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"no '## Agent Teams' heading directly above its table"* ]]
+    cmp "$F/before.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-8 lint-invariants passes the optional-table invariant on the live tree" {
+    run bash -c "cd '$R' && bash '$LINT' --json"
+    echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.message | test("agent_teams_constraints: table presence matches"))' >/dev/null
+    ! echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.level == "ERROR" and (.message | test("agent_teams")))' >/dev/null
+    # The field name is load-bearing: the negative check above is vacuous if
+    # the report shape ever renames `level`.
+    echo "$output" | jq -e '[.results[] | has("level")] | all' >/dev/null
+}
+
+@test "LI-9 the lint self-test (test-lint-invariants.sh) is green" {
+    run bash -c "cd '$R' && bash .claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh"
+    echo "$output" | tail -3
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}

+anchor = "## Agent-Network Primitives"

+         "<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->\n"

+         "<!-- @constraint-generated: end agent_teams_constraints -->\n\n")

+PY
+}

+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$output" = "0" ]

+
+@test "LI-2 the live kernel carries neither the Agent Teams heading nor its marker" {

+    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-3 the generator removes a leftover Agent Teams block when the class is empty" {

+    grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    run gen

+    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

+}
+
+@test "LI-7 a marker block with foreign text above it is an error, not a silent deletion" {

+    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'

+    echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.message | test("agent_teams_constraints: table presence matches"))' >/dev/null
+    ! echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.level == "ERROR" and (.message | test("agent_teams")))' >/dev/null

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/profile-floor.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
+# AC-9.2; SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166)
+#
+# No profile can reach the floor. The floor source is .claude/data/floor.yaml
+# (read here, never duplicated); its sha256 pin is READ from
+# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) so the two suites cannot
+# disagree. Under `lean` every floor surface reads byte-identically to
+# `standard`: the floor config keys (the two gate skills' flatline_protocol.*
+# config, destructive_command_guard.*, implement_gate.*, hounfour.locality),
+# verdict-derive.sh on fixture feedback files, the adversarial gate's
+# decision and environment, the deny-list file, the fence on the corpus and
+# the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes, and user-invoked-commands.txt.
+# =============================================================================
+
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
+    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+    FLOOR="$R/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    # Two configs that differ ONLY in loa.profile: this repository's own config
+    # (which carries the floor keys it really uses) with the profile set.
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        cp "$R/.loa.config.yaml" "$T/$p.yaml"
+        yq -i ".loa.profile = \"$p\"" "$T/$p.yaml"
+    done
+    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE LOA_PROFILES_FILE
+}
+
+# The floor key patterns, as the lib and the guard register read them.
+floor_keys() { yq -r '.floor_keys[]' "$FLOOR"; }
+
+@test "PF-1 floor.yaml matches the sha256 pin guard-origins.bats carries (one constant, two suites)" {
+    local pin actual
+    pin=$(sed -n 's/^FLOOR_SHA256="\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)"$/\1/p' "$R/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats")
+    [ -n "$pin" ] || { echo "no FLOOR_SHA256 in guard-origins.bats"; return 1; }
+    actual=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$2"' _ "$R" "$FLOOR" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+    [ "$actual" = "$pin" ] || { echo "floor.yaml sha256 $actual != pinned $pin"; return 1; }
+}
+
+@test "PF-2 no profiles.yaml key matches a floor key or is an ancestor of one" {
+    run python3 -I - "$PROFILES" "$FLOOR" <<'PY'
+import re, subprocess, sys, json
+def load(p):
+    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["yq", "-o=json", ".", p]))
+prof, floor = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
+keys = sorted({k for v in prof["profiles"].values() for k in v})
+assert len(keys) == 9, keys
+bad = []
+for k in keys:
+    for f in floor["floor_keys"]:
+        rx = "^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in f.split("*")) + "$"
+        if re.match(rx, k) or f.split("*")[0].startswith(k + "."):
+            bad.append((k, f))
+print("violations:", bad)
+sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
+PY
+    echo "$output"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    # floor_keys_forbidden is not duplicated into profiles.yaml.
+    [ "$(yq -r 'has("floor_keys_forbidden")' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
+}
+
+@test "PF-3 under lean the resolved document names no floor key and every floor key reads as under standard" {
+    local p k
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$LIB" json > "$T/$p.json"
+        [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/$p.json")" = "$p" ]
+    done
+    # Concrete floor keys: every leaf path of this config and the example that a
+    # floor pattern matches (flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice expands here).
+    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml" > "$T/cfg.json"
+    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example" > "$T/ex.json"
+    floor_keys > "$T/floor.txt"
+    python3 -I - "$T/cfg.json" "$T/ex.json" "$T/floor.txt" > "$T/concrete.txt" <<'PY'
+import json, re, sys
+pats = [l.strip() for l in open(sys.argv[3]) if l.strip()]
+rxs = ["^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in p.split("*")) + "$" for p in pats]
+out = set(p for p in pats if "*" not in p)
+def walk(x, path):
+    if isinstance(x, dict):
+        for k, v in x.items():
+            walk(v, path + [str(k)])
+    if path:
+        key = ".".join(path)
+        if any(re.match(r, key) for r in rxs):
+            out.add(key)
+for f in sys.argv[1:3]:
+    walk(json.load(open(f)), [])
+print("\n".join(sorted(k for k in out if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*", k))))
+PY
+    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    grep -q '^flatline_protocol\.[a-z_]*\.companion_voice$' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    while IFS= read -r k; do
+        [ "$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.knobs | has($k)' "$T/lean.json")" = "false" ] || { echo "lean resolves floor key $k"; return 1; }
+        a=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/lean.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
+        b=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/standard.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
+        [ "$a" = "$b" ] || { echo "$k: lean=$a standard=$b"; return 1; }
+    done < "$T/concrete.txt"
+    # The two gate skills' whole flatline_protocol config is byte-identical.
+    for g in code_review security_audit; do
+        cmp <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/lean.yaml") <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/standard.yaml")
+    done
+}
+
+@test "PF-4 verdict-derive.sh output is byte-identical under lean and standard" {
+    local f p
+    printf 'All good\n\n## Observations\n\n- **LOW** `a.sh:1` — naming\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":1},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/ok.md"
+    printf '## Changes Required\n\n- **HIGH** `a.sh:1` — unchecked input\n\nAll good\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/bad.md"
+    for f in ok bad; do
+        for p in lean standard; do
+            rc=0
+            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$R/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$T/$f.md" --gate review --json \
+                > "$T/vd-$f-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
+            echo "$rc" >> "$T/vd-$f-$p.out"
+        done
+        cmp "$T/vd-$f-lean.out" "$T/vd-$f-standard.out"
+    done
+    # The fixtures exercise both outcomes, so identity is not vacuous.
+    ! cmp -s "$T/vd-ok-lean.out" "$T/vd-bad-lean.out"
+}
+
+@test "PF-5 the adversarial-review gate decides identically under lean and standard" {
+    local d="$T/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-999" p rc
+    mkdir -p "$d"
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled = true' "$T/$p.yaml"
+        rc=0
+        printf '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s/COMPLETED"}}' "$d" \
+            | env -u LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_CONFIG_PATH_OVERRIDE="$T/$p.yaml" \
+              bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh" > "$T/gate-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
+        echo "$rc" >> "$T/gate-$p.out"
+    done
+    cmp "$T/gate-lean.out" "$T/gate-standard.out"
+    # No dissent envelope for an enabled gate: the gate refuses (exit 2) under both.
+    [ "$(tail -1 "$T/gate-lean.out")" = "2" ]
+    # The gate's environment knob is not a profile key and the gate never sources the lib.
+    ! grep -q 'profile-lib' "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh"
+    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qi 'adversarial'
+}
+
+@test "PF-6 the fence decides every corpus row and the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes identically under lean and standard" {
+    local p row cmd rc id
+    jq -r '.id' "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" > /dev/null
+    # Floor probes (the corpus carries the floor rules named in floor.yaml floor_corpus when they exist).
+    printf '%s\n' \
+        '{"id":"FP-1","cmd":"git stash pop 2>/dev/null"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-2","cmd":"git stash push -m x | tail -1"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-3","cmd":"echo x > .claude/hooks/evil.sh"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-4","cmd":"cp /tmp/a .claude/settings.json"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-5","cmd":"sed -i s/a/b/ .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"}' > "$T/probes.jsonl"
+    cat "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" "$T/probes.jsonl" > "$T/all.jsonl"
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        mkdir -p "$T/root-$p/repo"
+        cp "$T/$p.yaml" "$T/root-$p/.loa.config.yaml"
+        : > "$T/fence-$p.txt"
+        while IFS= read -r row; do
+            [ -n "$row" ] || continue
+            id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row")
+            rc=0
+            (cd "$T/root-$p/repo" && jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}' \
+                | env -u TMPDIR LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 LOA_REPO_ROOT="$T/root-$p" LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" \
+                  bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
+            echo "$id $rc" >> "$T/fence-$p.txt"
+        done < "$T/all.jsonl"
+    done
+    cmp "$T/fence-lean.txt" "$T/fence-standard.txt"
+    for id in FP-1 FP-2 FP-3 FP-4 FP-5; do
+        grep -qx "$id 2" "$T/fence-lean.txt" || { echo "$id not blocked under lean: $(grep "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt")"; return 1; }
+    done
+    # Every floor_corpus row present in the corpus is in the compared set.
+    while IFS= read -r rule; do
+        jq -r --arg r "$rule" 'select(.rule == $r or (($r | endswith("*")) and (.rule | startswith($r | rtrimstr("*"))))) | .id' \
+            "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" | while IFS= read -r id; do
+            grep -q "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt"
+        done
+    done < <(yq -r '.floor_corpus.rules[]' "$FLOOR")
+}
+
+@test "PF-7 the deny list, the System-Zone rules and user-invoked-commands.txt are untouched by resolving any profile" {
+    local f before after p
+    for f in .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt .claude/rules/zone-system.md .claude/data/floor.yaml; do
+        before=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$1/$2"' _ "$R" "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+        for p in lean standard; do
+            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/cache-$p.json" bash "$LIB" json >/dev/null
+        done
+        after=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$1/$2"' _ "$R" "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+        [ "$before" = "$after" ]
+    done
+    # The lib reads exactly three inputs and writes only its cache.
+    ! grep -Eq 'settings\.deny|user-invoked-commands|zone-system' "$LIB"
+    # The resolved documents differ only in the profile name and the profile-sourced values.
+    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/cache-lean.json")" = "lean" ]
+    [ "$(jq -c '.profile_keys' "$T/cache-lean.json")" = "$(jq -c '.profile_keys' "$T/cache-standard.json")" ]
+}

+    python3 -I - "$T/cfg.json" "$T/ex.json" "$T/floor.txt" > "$T/concrete.txt" <<'PY'
+import json, re, sys
+pats = [l.strip() for l in open(sys.argv[3]) if l.strip()]
+rxs = ["^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in p.split("*")) + "$" for p in pats]
+out = set(p for p in pats if "*" not in p)
+def walk(x, path):
+    if isinstance(x, dict):
+        for k, v in x.items():
+            walk(v, path + [str(k)])
+    if path:
+        key = ".".join(path)
+        if any(re.match(r, key) for r in rxs):
+            out.add(key)
+for f in sys.argv[1:3]:
+    walk(json.load(open(f)), [])
+print("\n".join(sorted(k for k in out if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*", k))))
+PY
+    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    grep -q '^flatline_protocol\.[a-z_]*\.companion_voice$' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    while IFS= read -r k; do
+        [ "$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.knobs | has($k)' "$T/lean.json")" = "false" ] || { echo "lean resolves floor key $k"; return 1; }
+        a=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/lean.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
+        b=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/standard.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
+        [ "$a" = "$b" ] || { echo "$k: lean=$a standard=$b"; return 1; }
+    done < "$T/concrete.txt"
+    # The two gate skills' whole flatline_protocol config is byte-identical.
+    for g in code_review security_audit; do
+        cmp <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/lean.yaml") <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/standard.yaml")
+    done
+}
+
+@test "PF-4 verdict-derive.sh output is byte-identical under lean and standard" {
+    local f p
+    printf 'All good\n\n## Observations\n\n- **LOW** `a.sh:1` — naming\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":1},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/ok.md"
+    printf '## Changes Required\n\n- **HIGH** `a.sh:1` — unchecked input\n\nAll good\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/bad.md"
+    for f in ok bad; do
+        for p in lean standard; do
+            rc=0
+            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$R/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$T/$f.md" --gate review --json \
+                > "$T/vd-$f-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
+            echo "$rc" >> "$T/vd-$f-$p.out"
+        done
+        cmp "$T/vd-$f-lean.out" "$T/vd-$f-standard.out"
+    done
+    # The fixtures exercise both outcomes, so identity is not vacuous.
+    ! cmp -s "$T/vd-ok-lean.out" "$T/vd-bad-lean.out"
+}
+
+@test "PF-5 the adversarial-review gate decides identically under lean and standard" {
+    local d="$T/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-999" p rc
+    mkdir -p "$d"
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled = true' "$T/$p.yaml"
+        rc=0
+        printf '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s/COMPLETED"}}' "$d" \
+            | env -u LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_CONFIG_PATH_OVERRIDE="$T/$p.yaml" \
+              bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh" > "$T/gate-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
+        echo "$rc" >> "$T/gate-$p.out"
+    done
+    cmp "$T/gate-lean.out" "$T/gate-standard.out"
+    # No dissent envelope for an enabled gate: the gate refuses (exit 2) under both.
+    [ "$(tail -1 "$T/gate-lean.out")" = "2" ]
+    # The gate's environment knob is not a profile key and the gate never sources the lib.
+    ! grep -q 'profile-lib' "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh"

+}
+
+@test "PF-6 the fence decides every corpus row and the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes identically under lean and standard" {
+    local p row cmd rc id
+    jq -r '.id' "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" > /dev/null
+    # Floor probes (the corpus carries the floor rules named in floor.yaml floor_corpus when they exist).
+    printf '%s\n' \
+        '{"id":"FP-1","cmd":"git stash pop 2>/dev/null"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-2","cmd":"git stash push -m x | tail -1"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-3","cmd":"echo x > .claude/hooks/evil.sh"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-4","cmd":"cp /tmp/a .claude/settings.json"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-5","cmd":"sed -i s/a/b/ .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"}' > "$T/probes.jsonl"
+    cat "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" "$T/probes.jsonl" > "$T/all.jsonl"
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        mkdir -p "$T/root-$p/repo"
+        cp "$T/$p.yaml" "$T/root-$p/.loa.config.yaml"
+        : > "$T/fence-$p.txt"
+        while IFS= read -r row; do
+            [ -n "$row" ] || continue
+            id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row")
+            rc=0
+            (cd "$T/root-$p/repo" && jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}' \
+                | env -u TMPDIR LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 LOA_REPO_ROOT="$T/root-$p" LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" \
+                  bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
+            echo "$id $rc" >> "$T/fence-$p.txt"
+        done < "$T/all.jsonl"
+    done
+    cmp "$T/fence-lean.txt" "$T/fence-standard.txt"
+    for id in FP-1 FP-2 FP-3 FP-4 FP-5; do
+        grep -qx "$id 2" "$T/fence-lean.txt" || { echo "$id not blocked under lean: $(grep "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt")"; return 1; }
+    done
+    # Every floor_corpus row present in the corpus is in the compared set.
+    while IFS= read -r rule; do
+        jq -r --arg r "$rule" 'select(.rule == $r or (($r | endswith("*")) and (.rule | startswith($r | rtrimstr("*"))))) | .id' \
+            "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" | while IFS= read -r id; do
+            grep -q "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt"
+        done
+    done < <(yq -r '.floor_corpus.rules[]' "$FLOOR")
+}
+
+@test "PF-7 the deny list, the System-Zone rules and user-invoked-commands.txt are untouched by resolving any profile" {
+    local f before after p
+    for f in .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt .claude/rules/zone-system.md .claude/data/floor.yaml; do

+        for p in lean standard; do
+            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/cache-$p.json" bash "$LIB" json >/dev/null
+        done
+        after=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$1/$2"' _ "$R" "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+        [ "$before" = "$after" ]
+    done

+    ! grep -Eq 'settings\.deny|user-invoked-commands|zone-system' "$LIB"

+++ b/tests/unit/profile-lib.bats
@@ -0,0 +1,258 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/profile-lib.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
+# AC-9.1, AC-9.3; SDD D-9.1, D-9.3)
+#
+# .claude/data/profiles.yaml + .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh: precedence
+# (explicit key > profile > fallback), every profile defines every key,
+# `standard` equals the oracle captured before any reader changed
+# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json), unknown profile, the
+# mtime-keyed cache, the overrides line, the /loa Profile line, the readers
+# that route through loa_knob, and the grep lint for direct reads.
+# =============================================================================
+
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
+    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+    ORACLE="$R/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    CFG="$T/config.yaml"
+    export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG"
+    export LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/run/effective-config.json"
+    : > "$CFG"
+}
+
+knob() { bash "$LIB" knob "$@"; }
+
+@test "PL-1 every profile defines every key, and the key set is the nine optional keys" {
+    run diff <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort) <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE" | sort)
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    for p in standard full; do
+        run diff <(yq -r ".profiles.$p | keys | .[]" "$PROFILES" | sort) <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort)
+        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    done
+    [ "$(yq -r '.profiles | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort | paste -sd, -)" = "full,lean,standard" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '.schema_version' "$PROFILES")" = "1" ]
+    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qx 'interview.pacing'
+}
+
+@test "PL-2 every profile value is a boolean; lean is all false and full all true" {
+    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles[][] | tag] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "!!bool" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.lean[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.full[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "true" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-3 standard equals the oracle captured before any reader changed" {
+    local k want got
+    while IFS= read -r k; do
+        want=$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.keys[$k].standard' "$ORACLE")
+        got=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")
+        [ "$want" = "$got" ] || { echo "standard $k = $got, oracle $want"; return 1; }
+    done < <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE")
+    # Outside the two guardrail keys (whose default this cycle changes) the
+    # oracle's standard IS the value the readers returned for the shipped example.
+    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.") | not)
+               | select(.value.standard != .value.example_today) | .key' "$ORACLE"
+    [ -z "$output" ]
+    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.")) | "\(.value.example_today)/\(.value.standard)"' "$ORACLE"
+    [ "$output" = "$(printf 'true/false\ntrue/false')" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-4 standard equals the post-cycle example defaults (explicit example value, else the reader's fallback)" {
+    local k ex st
+    while IFS= read -r k; do
+        ex=$(yq -r ".$k" "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example")
+        st=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")
+        if [ "$ex" = "null" ]; then
+            ex=$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.keys[$k].empty_config_today' "$ORACLE")
+        fi
+        [ "$ex" = "$st" ] || { echo "example $k = $ex, standard $st"; return 1; }
+    done < <(yq -r '.profiles.standard | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES")
+    [ "$(yq -r '.loa.profile' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example")" = "standard" ]
+    # Under the example config the lib resolves standard and no override.
+    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$R/.loa.config.yaml.example" run bash "$LIB" overrides
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ -z "$output" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-5 precedence: explicit key beats the profile, the profile beats the fallback" {
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nknown_failures:\n  surface_at_session_start: true\nkarpathy_principles:\n  diff_lines_per_task: 250\n' > "$CFG"
+    [ "$(knob known_failures.surface_at_session_start false)" = "true" ]     # explicit
+    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start true)" = "false" ]          # lean, not the fallback
+    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true)" = "false" ]   # lean
+    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100)" = "250" ]        # non-profile key, explicit
+    [ "$(knob run_mode.stale_hours 7)" = "7" ]                               # non-profile key, fallback
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
+    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start false)" = "true" ]
+    : > "$CFG"
+    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile)" = "standard" ]
+    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source)" = "default" ]
+    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning false)" = "true" ]   # standard, not the fallback
+}
+
+@test "PL-6 an explicit false is honoured (yq's // would read it as absent)" {
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: false\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: false\n' > "$CFG"
+    [ "$(knob guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(knob guardrails.danger_level.enforce true)" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(knob .guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]                   # leading dot accepted
+}
+
+@test "PL-7 an unknown profile warns once on stderr and resolves standard" {
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: turbo\n' > "$CFG"
+    run --separate-stderr bash "$LIB" profile
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$output" = "standard" ]
+    [[ "$stderr" == *'unknown loa.profile "turbo"; using standard'* ]]
+    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source 2>/dev/null)" = "invalid" ]
+    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria false 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ]
+    # A non-string profile is unknown too.
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: [lean]\n' > "$CFG"
+    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile 2>/dev/null)" = "standard" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-8 the cache is written once and rebuilt when the config or profiles.yaml changes" {
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\n' > "$CFG"
+    touch -d '2026-01-01 00:00:00' "$CFG"
+    knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x >/dev/null
+    [ -f "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "lean" ]
+    # Same stamps → served from the cache: a planted value proves the read path.
+    jq '.knobs["decisions.surface_at_session_start"].value = "from-cache"' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
+    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "from-cache" ]
+    # A config edit with a new mtime rebuilds.
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
+    touch -d '2026-01-02 00:00:00' "$CFG"
+    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "true" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "full" ]
+    # A profiles.yaml edit rebuilds too.
+    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/profiles.yaml"
+    export LOA_PROFILES_FILE="$T/profiles.yaml"
+    knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x >/dev/null
+    yq -i '.profiles.full["decisions.surface_at_session_start"] = false' "$T/profiles.yaml"
+    touch -d '2026-01-03 00:00:00' "$T/profiles.yaml"
+    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "false" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-9 a corrupt or foreign cache file is rebuilt, never trusted" {
+    mkdir -p "$T/run"
+    echo 'not json' > "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
+    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning x)" = "true" ]
+    jq -e '.schema_version == 1' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" >/dev/null
+    jq '.id = "other"' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
+    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning x)" = "true" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.id' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" != "other" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-10 a seam config without a cache seam writes no cache (the repository cache is never touched)" {
+    unset LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
+    mkdir -p "$T/root/.claude/data"
+    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+    LOA_PROFILE_ROOT="$T/root" run bash "$LIB" knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x
+    [ "$output" = "false" ]
+    [ ! -e "$T/root/.run/effective-config.json" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-11 overrides lists the explicit profile keys that differ from the profile, sorted" {
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\ndecisions:\n  surface_at_session_start: false\nstructured_handoff:\n  enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
+    run bash "$LIB" overrides
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$output" = "$(printf 'guardrails.input.enabled=true\nstructured_handoff.enabled=true')" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-12 a profiles.yaml key that names a floor key is ignored with a WARN" {
+    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/profiles.yaml"
+    yq -i '.profiles.standard["implement_gate.mode"] = "deny" | .profiles.standard["flatline_protocol"] = false' "$T/profiles.yaml"
+    export LOA_PROFILES_FILE="$T/profiles.yaml"
+    run --separate-stderr bash "$LIB" knob implement_gate.mode ask
+    [ "$output" = "ask" ]
+    [[ "$stderr" == *"profiles.yaml key implement_gate.mode names a floor key; ignored"* ]]
+    [[ "$stderr" == *"profiles.yaml key flatline_protocol names a floor key; ignored"* ]]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.profile_keys | index("implement_gate.mode")' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "null" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-13 a malformed key path returns 2 with the fallback and never reaches yq" {
+    printf 'a: 1\n' > "$CFG"
+    run bash "$LIB" knob '.a | env' fb
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"fb"* ]]
+    run bash "$LIB" knob 'a;b' fb
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-14 the /loa Profile line prints the profile and the explicit overrides" {
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
+    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE
+    run --separate-stderr env CACHE_DIR="$T/wscache" LOA_STATUS_RUN_DIR="$T/srun" LOA_STATUS_ENV_DIR="$T/env" \
+        LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG" timeout 120 bash "$R/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh" --no-stale-check
+    line=$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep '^Profile:')
+    [ "$line" = "Profile: lean (explicit overrides: guardrails.input.enabled=true)" ]
+    : > "$CFG"
+    run --separate-stderr env CACHE_DIR="$T/wscache" LOA_STATUS_RUN_DIR="$T/srun" LOA_STATUS_ENV_DIR="$T/env" \
+        LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG" timeout 120 bash "$R/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh" --no-stale-check
+    line=$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep '^Profile:')
+    [ "$line" = "Profile: standard (explicit overrides: none)" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-15 the guardrail readers route through loa_knob (knob on and off)" {
+    printf 'guardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: false\n' > "$CFG"
+    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh" --skill implementing-tasks --input "Implement feature X"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.reason')" = "guardrails disabled in config" ]
+    printf 'guardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
+    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh" --skill implementing-tasks --input "Implement feature X"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.reason')" != "guardrails disabled in config" ]
+    printf 'guardrails:\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: false\n' > "$CFG"
+    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/danger-level-enforcer.sh" --skill deploying-infrastructure --mode autonomous
+    [[ "$output" == *"danger level enforcement disabled in config"* ]]
+    printf 'guardrails:\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: true\n' > "$CFG"
+    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/danger-level-enforcer.sh" --skill deploying-infrastructure --mode autonomous
+    [[ "$output" != *"danger level enforcement disabled in config"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "PL-16 the SessionStart readers resolve their enable key through the profile" {
+    # `full` turns the decisions and KF surfaces on without their keys; an
+    # explicit false beats the profile; `standard` leaves them off.
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
+    run bash "$R/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"[DECISIONS]"* ]]
+    run bash "$R/.claude/hooks/loa-kf-surface.sh"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"[KF-SURFACE]"* ]]
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\ndecisions:\n  surface_at_session_start: false\nknown_failures:\n  surface_at_session_start: false\n' > "$CFG"
+    run bash "$R/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ -z "$output" ]
+    run bash "$R/.claude/hooks/loa-kf-surface.sh"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ -z "$output" ]
+    : > "$CFG"
+    run bash "$R/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh"

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/profile-lib.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD

+#
+# .claude/data/profiles.yaml + .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh: precedence

+# `standard` equals the oracle captured before any reader changed

+# =============================================================================

+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
+    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+    ORACLE="$R/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json"

+    : > "$CFG"
+}
+
+knob() { bash "$LIB" knob "$@"; }
+
+@test "PL-1 every profile defines every key, and the key set is the nine optional keys" {
+    run diff <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort) <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE" | sort)
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    for p in standard full; do
+        run diff <(yq -r ".profiles.$p | keys | .[]" "$PROFILES" | sort) <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort)
+        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    done
+    [ "$(yq -r '.profiles | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort | paste -sd, -)" = "full,lean,standard" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '.schema_version' "$PROFILES")" = "1" ]
+    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qx 'interview.pacing'

+
+@test "PL-2 every profile value is a boolean; lean is all false and full all true" {
+    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles[][] | tag] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "!!bool" ]

+    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.full[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "true" ]

+@test "PL-3 standard equals the oracle captured before any reader changed" {

+        got=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")

+    done < <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE")

+    # oracle's standard IS the value the readers returned for the shipped example.
+    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.") | not)
+               | select(.value.standard != .value.example_today) | .key' "$ORACLE"
+    [ -z "$output" ]
+    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.")) | "\(.value.example_today)/\(.value.standard)"' "$ORACLE"
+    [ "$output" = "$(printf 'true/false\ntrue/false')" ]

+        fi

+    done < <(yq -r '.profiles.standard | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES")

+@test "PL-5 precedence: explicit key beats the profile, the profile beats the fallback" {

+    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning x)" = "true" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.id' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" != "other" ]

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-derive.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.10
+# (PRD FR-5 AC-5.1 … AC-5.4, FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-5.1, D-5.1a, D-5.2, D-5.3, D-5.4)
+# `run-checkpoint.sh derive` rebuilds the run position from files: one case per
+# decision-table row, the breaker recompute from the feedback history, the
+# write path and its rollback knob, and one case per known reader over a
+# derived file. Fixture: a tiny git repo with a ledger, a2a/ and .run/ in a
+# temp dir; nothing touches this checkout's .run/.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcd.XXXXXX")"
+  R="$T/repo"
+  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a" "$R/.run" "$R/src"
+  git -C "$R" init -q
+  printf 'x\n' > "$R/src/a.ts"
+  git -C "$R" add -A
+  git -C "$R" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid commit -qm "feat: impl"
+  ledger completed completed completed
+  unset LOA_RUN_DIR LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE
+}
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+# ledger STATUS101 STATUS102 STATUS103 [EXTRA-SPRINT-JSON]
+ledger() {
+  jq -n --arg a "$1" --arg b "$2" --arg c "$3" --argjson x "${4:-null}" '
+    {schema_version: 1, active_cycle: "cycle-x", next_sprint_number: 104,
+     cycles: [
+       {id: "cycle-old", status: "archived", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
+        sprints: [{global_id: 1, local_label: "sprint-1", status: "completed", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]},
+       {id: "cycle-x", status: "active", created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
+        sprints: ([{global_id: 101, local_label: "sprint-1", status: $a, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
+                   {global_id: 102, local_label: "sprint-2", status: $b, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
+                   {global_id: 103, local_label: "sprint-3", status: $c, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]
+                  + (if $x == null then [] else [$x] end))}]}' > "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
+}
+
+# feedback GID GATE VERDICT [SPRINT_ID] [ROUND] [MEDIUM] [TS] — a feedback file whose trailer verdict-derive accepts
+feedback() {
+  local gid="$1" gate="$2" verdict="$3" sid="${4:-sprint-$1}" round="${5:-}" med="${6:-0}" ts="${7:-2026-06-01T00:00:00Z}" f prose
+  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid"
+  if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then f=engineer-feedback; else f=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
+  [[ -n "$round" ]] && f="$f-r$round"
+  if [[ "$verdict" == APPROVED ]]; then
+    if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
+  else
+    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: something to fix'
+  fi
+  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"%s","ts":"%s"} -->\n' \
+    "$prose" "$gate" "$verdict" "$med" "$sid" "$ts" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid/$f.md"
+}
+
+# complete GID [SPRINT_ID] — review + audit APPROVED and the COMPLETED marker
+complete() {
+  feedback "$1" review APPROVED "${2:-}"
+  feedback "$1" audit APPROVED "${2:-}"
+  printf 'COMPLETED 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z\nsprint: %s\n' "${2:-sprint-$1}" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$1/COMPLETED"
+}
+
+# cache STATE [AGE_HOURS] [EXTRA-JQ] — .run/sprint-plan-state.json (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
+cache() {
+  jq -n --arg s "$1" --argjson h "${2:-0}" '
+    {schema_version: 2, plan_id: "plan-x", branch: "feature/x", state: $s,
+     timestamps: {started: "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z", last_activity: (now - $h * 3600 | floor | todate)},
+     sprints: {total: 3, completed: 0, current: "sprint-1",
+               list: [{id: "sprint-1", status: "in_progress"}, {id: "sprint-2", status: "pending"}, {id: "sprint-3", status: "pending"}]}}
+    '"${3:+| $3}" > "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+}
+
+derive() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" derive --root "$R" "$@"; }
+_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
+dj() { jq -r "$1" <<<"$output"; }
+
+# --- decision table: run state -------------------------------------------------
+
+@test "RCD-1 drift fixture (D-5.4): cache RUNNING, three COMPLETED markers with APPROVED trailers, ledger completed → COMPLETE; --write makes the cache say so" {
+  complete 101; complete 102; complete 103
+  cache RUNNING
+  derive --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = COMPLETE ]
+  [ "$(dj '.cache_state')" = RUNNING ]
+  [ "$(dj '.drift')" = true ]
+  [ "$(dj '[.sprints[].state] | join(",")')" = "complete,complete,complete" ]
+  [ "$(dj '[.sprints[].completed_marker] | all')" = true ]
+  [ "$(dj '.written')" = false ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .state "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json")" = RUNNING ]   # --json alone writes nothing
+  derive --json --write
+  [ "$(dj '.written')" = true ]
+  run jq -r '[.state, .status, (.derived_at | test("^20[0-9]{2}-")), .derivation.source, .schema_version, .plan_id, .sprints.total] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+  [ "$output" = "COMPLETE COMPLETE true files 2 plan-x 3" ]
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.drift')" = false ]
+  [ -z "$(find "$R/.run" -name '*.tmp.*')" ]
+}
+
+@test "RCD-2 a stale marker whose trailers name sprint-1 of another cycle (or whose sprint: line names another sprint) is stale_marker, not counted" {
+  complete 101; complete 102; complete 103 sprint-1
+  cache RUNNING
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[2] | [.marker_present, .stale_marker, .completed_marker, .state] | map(tostring) | join(" ")')" = "true true false in_progress" ]
+  [ "$(dj '.derivation.stale_markers | join(",")')" = "sprint-103" ]
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = RUNNING ]
+  [[ "$(dj '.notes | join(";")')" == *"sprint-103: COMPLETED marker names another sprint"* ]]
+  # trailers right, marker line wrong → still stale
+  complete 103
+  printf 'COMPLETED x\nsprint: sprint-7\n' > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-103/COMPLETED"
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[2].stale_marker')" = true ]
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[2].state')" = awaiting_marker ]
+  # the local label is this sprint's name too
+  complete 103 sprint-3
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[2].state')" = complete ]
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = COMPLETE ]
+}
+
+@test "RCD-3 legacy feedback (no LOA-VERDICT trailer) yields no verdict: the sprint stays incomplete and the file is named in derivation.legacy_feedback" {
+  complete 101; complete 102; complete 103
+  printf 'All good\n' > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-103/engineer-feedback.md"
+  cache RUNNING
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[2].review.verdict')" = null ]
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[2].state')" = in_progress ]
+  [ "$(dj '.derivation.legacy_feedback | join(",")')" = "grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-103/engineer-feedback.md" ]
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = RUNNING ]
+  derive --write
+  [ "$(jq -r '.derivation.legacy_feedback[0]' "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json")" = "grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-103/engineer-feedback.md" ]
+}
+
+@test "RCD-4 review and audit APPROVED without a marker is awaiting_marker (counted incomplete); a marker with the ledger row not completed is in_progress" {
+  complete 101; complete 102
+  feedback 103 review APPROVED; feedback 103 audit APPROVED
+  cache RUNNING
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[2].state')" = awaiting_marker ]
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = RUNNING ]
+  printf 'COMPLETED x\n' > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-103/COMPLETED"
+  ledger completed completed in_progress
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[2] | [.completed_marker, .state] | map(tostring) | join(" ")')" = "true in_progress" ]
+  # an inconsistent APPROVED trailer (verdict-derive exit 1) is not APPROVED
+  ledger completed completed completed
+  printf 'Looks fine\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-103","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-103/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[2].audit.consistent')" = false ]
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[2].state')" = in_progress ]
+}
+
+@test "RCD-5 JACKED_OUT is terminal: a cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha, stays JACKED_OUT with contradicting files reported as drift" {
+  complete 101
+  cache JACKED_OUT 30
+  derive --json --write
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = JACKED_OUT ]
+  [[ "$(dj '.notes | join(";")')" == *"JACKED_OUT is terminal"* ]]
+  [ "$(jq -r .state "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json")" = JACKED_OUT ]
+  # the cycle-128 defect shape: .state RUNNING, .status JACKED_OUT
+  cache RUNNING 0 '.status = "JACKED_OUT"'
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = JACKED_OUT ]
+  [ "$(dj '.drift')" = true ]
+  [[ "$(dj '.notes | join(";")')" == *"cache .state RUNNING and .status JACKED_OUT disagree"* ]]
+  cache RUNNING 0 '.completion = {merged_sha: "abc123"}'
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = JACKED_OUT ]
+  cache RUNNING 0 '.completion = {merged_sha: null}'
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = RUNNING ]
+}
+
+@test "RCD-6 HALTED is sticky: a cache HALTED stays HALTED even when every sprint is complete; a breaker OPEN halts a RUNNING cache" {
+  complete 101; complete 102; complete 103
+  cache HALTED
+  derive --json --write
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = HALTED ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.state + " " + .status' "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json")" = "HALTED HALTED" ]
+  rm -rf "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-103"
+  cache RUNNING
+  printf '{"state":"OPEN","triggers":{"same_issue":{"count":0,"threshold":3,"last_hash":null},"no_progress":{"count":0,"threshold":5},"cycle_count":{"current":0,"limit":20},"timeout":{"started":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z","limit_hours":8}},"history":[]}\n' > "$R/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = HALTED ]
+  [ "$(dj '.breaker.state')" = OPEN ]
+}
+
+@test "RCD-7 COMPLETE never moves back to RUNNING unless the ledger registers a new incomplete sprint" {
+  complete 101; complete 102; complete 103
+  cache RUNNING
+  derive --write
+  [ "$(jq -r .state "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json")" = COMPLETE ]
+  [ "$(jq -c .derivation.sprint_ids "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json")" = '["sprint-101","sprint-102","sprint-103"]' ]
+  jq '.timestamps.last_activity = (now | floor | todate)' "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+  rm "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-103/COMPLETED"
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = COMPLETE ]
+  [[ "$(dj '.notes | join(";")')" == *"COMPLETE kept"* ]]
+  ledger completed completed completed '{"global_id": 104, "local_label": "sprint-4", "status": "planned", "created": "2026-01-02T00:00:00Z"}'
+  complete 103
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = RUNNING ]
+  [ "$(dj '.sprints[3].state')" = in_progress ]
+}
+
+@test "RCD-8 an incomplete sprint is RUNNING while last_activity is within run_mode.stale_hours (default 12), else INTERRUPTED; the key widens the window" {
+  complete 101
+  cache RUNNING 1
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = RUNNING ]
+  cache RUNNING 13
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = INTERRUPTED ]
+  [ "$(dj '.stale_hours')" = 12 ]
+  command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"
+  printf 'run_mode:\n  stale_hours: 24\n' > "$R/.loa.config.yaml"
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.state')" = RUNNING ]
+  [ "$(dj '.stale_hours')" = 24 ]
+  # no cache at all: the derivation is reported, nothing is written
+  rm "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+  derive --json --write
+  [ "$(dj '.cache')" = missing ]
+  [ "$(dj '.written')" = false ]
+  [ ! -e "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ]
+}
+
+# --- breaker recompute (D-4.6 mechanical caller) ------------------------------
+
+@test "RCD-9 breaker recompute: two -r1 feedback files and a zeroed breaker give cycle_count 2, same_issue 2, no_progress 1; counters are raised, never lowered" {
+  complete 101
+  feedback 102 review CHANGES_REQUIRED sprint-102 1 1 2026-06-01T01:00:00Z
+  feedback 102 audit CHANGES_REQUIRED sprint-102 1 1 2026-06-01T02:00:00Z
+  feedback 102 review APPROVED
+  cache RUNNING
+  printf '{"state":"CLOSED","triggers":{"same_issue":{"count":0,"threshold":3,"last_hash":null},"no_progress":{"count":0,"threshold":5},"cycle_count":{"current":0,"limit":20},"timeout":{"started":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z","limit_hours":8}},"history":[]}\n' > "$R/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
+  derive --json
+  [ "$(dj '.active_sprint')" = sprint-102 ]
+  [ "$(dj '.breaker.recomputed | [.cycle_count, .same_issue, .no_progress] | map(tostring) | join(" ")')" = "2 2 1" ]
+  derive --write
+  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.no_progress.count, (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$R/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
+  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 2 2 1 32" ]
+  # the recorded hash is the run-mode same-issue hash of the last round
+  local want

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.5
+# (PRD FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-4.6). `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` replaces the
+# run-mode SKILL's breaker prose: the same-issue hash from the derived verdict,
+# no-progress, cycle count, timeout; a trip writes OPEN + HALTED and exits 10.
+# All files live in a temp dir.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
+  VD="$REPO/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcr.XXXXXX")"
+  mkdir -p "$T/.run" "$T/a2a"
+  B="$T/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
+  S="$T/.run/state.json"
+  printf '{"run_id":"r","state":"RUNNING","phase":"REVIEW"}\n' > "$S"
+}
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+# fb NAME GATE VERDICT [MEDIUM] — a feedback file verdict-derive accepts
+fb() {
+  local prose
+  if [[ "$3" == APPROVED ]]; then
+    if [[ "$2" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
+  else
+    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: fix it'
+  fi
+  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' \
+    "$prose" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" > "$T/a2a/$1"
+}
+
+_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
+
+breaker() {  # $1 jq tweak over a CLOSED breaker started now
+  jq -n '{state: "CLOSED",
+          triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: 3, last_hash: null}, no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: 5},
+                     cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: 20}, timeout: {started: (now | floor | todate), limit_hours: 8}},
+          history: []}'"${1:+ | $1}" > "$B"
+}
+
+rr() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" record-round --root "$T" --breaker "$B" --state-file "$S" --sprint sprint-1 "$@"; }
+
+@test "RCR-1 a CHANGES_REQUIRED review increments cycle_count.current, sets same_issue {count 1, last_hash} to the SKILL's derived hash, exit 0" {
+  breaker
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review CHANGES_REQUIRED — cycle 1/20, same_issue 1/3, no_progress 0/5" ]]
+  local want
+  want=$(bash "$VD" --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>/dev/null | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
+  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.same_issue.last_hash, (.history | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
+  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 1 $want 0" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-2 the same hash again counts up; a different finding set resets same_issue to 1 with the new last_hash" {
+  breaker
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 2 ]
+  local h1; h1=$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 2
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 1 ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")" != "$h1" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.cycle_count.current "$B")" = 3 ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-3 no_progress counts consecutive rounds whose counts are unchanged and resets when they change" {
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99'
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 0 ]
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 2 ]
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 3
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-4 a trip at threshold writes state OPEN, appends one history entry, sets .run/state.json HALTED, prints TRIPPED and exits 10" {
+  breaker
+  fb auditor-sprint-feedback.md audit CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *$'\n'"TRIPPED: same_issue: same issue hash "*" seen 3 times in a row" ]]
+  run jq -r '[.state, (.history | length), .history[0].trigger, .history[0].gate, .history[0].sprint] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
+  [ "$output" = "OPEN 1 same_issue audit sprint-1" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.state + " " + .run_id' "$S")" = "HALTED r" ]
+  # a further round on an OPEN breaker still exits 10 and does not duplicate the history entry
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.history | length' "$B")" = 1 ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-5 the cycle limit, the no-progress threshold and the timeout trip in that documented order" {
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 19'
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: cycle_count: 20 changes-required rounds reached the limit 20" ]]
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 4 | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = "{\"critical\":0,\"high\":0,\"medium\":1,\"low\":0}"'
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: no_progress: "* ]]
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.timeout.started = (now - 9 * 3600 | floor | todate)'
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: timeout: run older than 8 hours" ]]
+  [ "$(jq -r .history[-1].trigger "$B")" = timeout ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats

+# (PRD FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-4.6). `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` replaces the
+# run-mode SKILL's breaker prose: the same-issue hash from the derived verdict,
+# no-progress, cycle count, timeout; a trip writes OPEN + HALTED and exits 10.
+# All files live in a temp dir.

+  B="$T/.run/circuit-breaker.json"

+}
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

+# fb NAME GATE VERDICT [MEDIUM] — a feedback file verdict-derive accepts
+fb() {
+  local prose
+  if [[ "$3" == APPROVED ]]; then

+    "$prose" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" > "$T/a2a/$1"

+_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

compute_hash() {
  local file="${1:-}"

  if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then
    echo ""
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    # Empty file hash
    echo "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"
    return 0
  fi

  local ext="${file##*.}"
  local content=""

  case "$ext" in
    sh)
      # For shell: skip shebang (line 1) and marker/warning (lines 2-3)
      if head -1 "$file" | grep -q "^#!"; then
        content=$(tail -n +4 "$file")
      else
        # No shebang, skip first 2 lines (marker + warning)
        content=$(tail -n +3 "$file")
      fi

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is sprint-256 (`pr/head.diff`, 68 files): the implement gate's three modes and marker sanction, the file-authoritative run position in `run-checkpoint.sh` (`derive`, `record-round`, `mark`), the heredoc consumer classifier in the Bash fence, the `loa.profile` resolver, the C-TEAM rows moved out of the kernel, and the per-task surgical-diff hook. The design is coherent and the test matrices are unusually thorough; the fence corpus passes completely with the classifier on (89/89 benign, 142/142 dangerous), the implement-gate mode matrix passes (IG-24 to IG-33, 10/10), `profile-lib.bats` passes 17/17 and `lint-invariants.bats` 9/9 in a scratch head tree, the managed-header hash of `CLAUDE.loa.md` verifies, and the kernel fits the new 9,445 B cap (9,189 B).

Three defects block the merge. First, the classifier's `nonexec` class drops heredoc bodies for write targets it does not recognise as executable, and two commands the base hook blocked now pass (a cron drop-in written through `/tmp/../etc/`, and a `package.json` script body followed by `npm run`). Second, `run-checkpoint.sh derive` does not run at all on jq 1.6 (the version installed here and in Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04) because the per-sprint jq program binds `$label`, a jq keyword; 13 of the 22 `run-checkpoint-derive.bats` cases fail and every `write` prints jq errors. Third, the breaker recompute counts trailer-less "All good" rounds as changes-required rounds with identical hashes, so three legacy approved files in the active sprint directory trip the breaker and flip a RUNNING run to HALTED on its first checkpoint (demonstrated with a working `fb_parse`).

Verification limits: the eval workspace carries no `tests/` tree, so suites that need fixtures outside the PR (`pretooluse-payloads/`, `guard-origins.bats`, `constraint-rationales-pre-diet.json`) and the two karpathy suites (whose secret literal the snapshot redacted into a syntax error) could not be run; the validator and the prompt-budget tool were exercised by hand instead and behaved as their new tests expect.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Safety fence: `nonexec` heredoc bodies are dropped for targets the classifier does not recognise as executable (regression against the base hook)

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:303-325` — `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` judges the write target by literal prefix and extension only; a target that a later command executes but that is not a script, rc file, `.claude/hooks`, `.git/hooks`, `/etc/...` or a PATH directory is classed non-executing, its body is reduced to fence-verb segments, and destructive content inside it is never scanned.
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:303-325`, the lists at `:189-190`, the `/etc` prefix test at `:312`, the segment drop at `:576-604`

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is sprint-256 (`pr/head.diff`, 68 files): the implement gate's three modes and marker sanction, the file-authoritative run position in `run-checkpoint.sh` (`derive`, `record-round`, `mark`), the heredoc consumer classifier in the Bash fence, the `loa.profile` resolver, the C-TEAM rows moved out of the kernel, and the per-task surgical-diff hook. Three defects block the merge. First, the classifier's `nonexec` class drops heredoc bodies for write targets it does not recognise as executable, and two command shapes the base hook blocked now pass (a cron drop-in reached through a `..` path segment, and a `package.json` scripts entry executed by a following `npm run`). ---

**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:303-325` (the lists at `:189-190`, the unnormalised `/etc` prefix test at `:312`, the segment drop at `:593`)
**Issue:** Replayed through both hooks in scratch trees (head and base), two shapes flip from block (exit 2) to allow (exit 0):

**Reference:** CWE-184 (incomplete list of disallowed inputs), CWE-22 (path traversal in the destination test).

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378-389` — the `sj=$(jq -nc … --arg label "$label" …)` program references `$label`; `label` is a jq keyword and jq 1.6 rejects `$label` with `syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__`, so `cmd_derive` never produces a sprint row.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378-389`
**Issue:** On this machine (jq-1.6) `derive --json` exits non-zero with two compile errors, `write` (which now runs `derive --write` at `:174`) prints the jq errors on every checkpoint, `mark` does the same (`:541`), and the `/loa` Run line (`loa-status.sh:1016-1021`) never appears. - **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:276-284` — `recompute` counts every round whose `approved` is false, and `fb_parse` marks any trailer-less file unapproved (`:233-238`) with a hash taken from its findings section (`:230`); an "All good" file without a trailer has no findings section, so every such file hashes to the md5 of the empty string, three of them give `same_issue` 3, `merge_breaker` opens the breaker (`:300-311`), and `resolve` derives HALTED.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:276-284` (hash at `:230`, automatic `derive --write` from `write` at `:174` and from `mark` at `:541`)
**Issue:** Reproduced with a copy of the script whose `$label` and empty-trailer fallbacks were patched so the code path runs: a fixture repo with one in-progress sprint, three legacy `engineer-feedback-rN.md` files reading "All good", a current approved file with a trailer, and a fresh RUNNING cache; `derive --write` reports `breaker.recomputed {cycle_count: 3, same_issue: 3}`, writes `state: OPEN`, `trigger: same_issue`, and rewrites the cache to HALTED. **Required Fix:** In `recompute`, exclude rounds with `trailer: false` (they already surface under `legacy_feedback`), or at least exclude a legacy file whose findings-section hash is the empty-input md5 and whose first line is the approval phrase; never let two legacy files with no findings section compare equal. ---

### 1. `--file` outside a `.run/` directory writes the repository's own breaker

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:108-117` — when `--file` does not sit in a directory named `.run`, `root` falls back to the script's checkout and `breaker` to that checkout's `.run/circuit-breaker.json`, so `write --file /tmp/x/state.json …` (reproduced) creates and updates the real repository's breaker from the real ledger while the caller believes it is working on a scratch file.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:108-117`, the derive call at `:174`
**Suggestion:** Derive `run_dir` from the directory of `--file` whatever its name, or refuse `derive --write` when `--file` and `run_dir` disagree.
**Benefit:** No cross-contamination of live run state from tests or ad-hoc calls.

### 2. The trailer and verdict-derive fallbacks rely on `jq -e` failing on empty input

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226` (and `:223`) — `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'` never fires when `$pj` is empty, because `jq -e` exits 0 with no input (verified on jq 1.6); a trailer-less file then reaches `--argjson p ""`, `fb_parse` emits nothing, the round silently vanishes from `rounds_of`, and `record-round` on a legacy file exits 3 (`RCR-7` fails here). **Suggestion:** Test `[[ -n "$pj" ]]` before the `jq -e` check (same for `$vj`).
**Benefit:** Deterministic behaviour across jq versions; legacy rounds are either counted or excluded by design, never dropped by accident.

### 3. The fence-verb list and the same-line executor check are narrower than the contract states

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:214-220` — `_bdb_hd_is_destructive` is a hand-maintained list described as "command words the fence's own rules match", yet the rule set also keys on `sed -i`, `cp`, `mv`, redirections into `.claude/`, `docker`, `npm`, `make` and others; a `nonexec` body carrying those words is dropped before the normal rules run. `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` (`:608-640`) also treats `cat` as a safe reader inside process substitution, so a target fed to `source <(cat target)` on a later line is not recognised as executed (companion dissent DISS-C-004 and DISS-C-005).
**Suggestion:** Derive the verb list from the rule table (or assert equality in `run-corpus.sh`), and in `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` return interpreter-class when a line naming the target also holds `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(`, mirroring `_bdb_hd_ctx_bad`.
**Benefit:** The classifier's fail-closed contract holds as rules evolve.

### 4. "Turning the classifier off only tightens" is not what the corpus shows

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1243` and `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:732` — with `--knob-off`, `run-corpus.sh` reports 4 dangerous rows allowed that the classifier blocks (D127, D131, D136, D141) and 5 benign rows blocked; the rollback key is looser in one direction and tighter in the other.
**Suggestion:** Reword to "restores the pre-cycle scan" and list the four FR-6 rows the pre-cycle scan misses.
**Benefit:** An operator rolling back knows what coverage they lose.

### 5. The profile cache in `.run/` is consulted before the configuration

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:67` and `:219-243` — `loa_knob` serves `.run/effective-config.json` whenever its id matches the config's stat line; a Bash-written cache with the right id flips any profile key (both guardrail knobs included) without touching `.loa.config.yaml`. Same trust class as the other `.run/` inputs the PR documents (bd-taee), but not named anywhere.
**Suggestion:** Document the cache under the accepted `.run/` gaps, or key the id on a content hash of the config rather than its mtime and size.
**Benefit:** The trust boundary of the profile layer is stated where the others are.

### 6. The surgical-diff hook forks `run-checkpoint.sh read` (and `br show`) on every Write/Edit

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131` — each counted write spawns bash + the checkpoint reader, which itself runs `br show` when a task checkpoint exists; the design note says the perf caches were removed because per-task files are small, but this new per-write fork is the larger cost.
**Suggestion:** Cache the resolved key in the summary file keyed on the checkpoint file's mtime, or read `.checkpoint.task` with one jq and skip the beads confirmation in the hook (the review's SURGICAL axis is advisory).
**Benefit:** Keeps the PostToolUse path within the hook latency budget.

### 7. `_ig_within` rejects ISO timestamps with a UTC offset

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:475-481` — `fromdateiso8601` parses only a trailing `Z`; a `derived_at` or `started_at` written as `+00:00` is treated as stale, so a sanction silently disappears (companion dissent DISS-C-002). Every writer in this PR uses `Z`, so no live path fails today.
**Suggestion:** Normalise `+00:00` / `-00:00` to `Z` before parsing.
**Benefit:** Robust against other writers of the same state files.

### 8. Two safety defaults flip to off with no migration notice

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:36-38` and `head/.claude/scripts/danger-level-enforcer.sh:139-143` — `guardrails.input.enabled` and `guardrails.danger_level.enforce` now resolve to false for every repository that never set them (DEC-0161 is cited; the change is intentional), and nothing at session start or on the `/loa` Profile line tells an upgrading operator that enforcement they had is now off (companion dissent DISS-C-003).
**Suggestion:** Print a one-time note on the Profile line when `loa.profile` is unset and neither key is explicit.
**Benefit:** The default flip is visible where the operator looks.
